extract:primary-0005-121416e6bb.summary: Alice’s encounter with the Caterpillar centers on unstable identity, faulty memory, and size-changing advice. After learning that the Mushroom can alter her height, she experiments until her neck rises above the trees, prompting a Pigeon to attack her as a supposed serpent. Alice finally regains her usual height and then makes herself small enough to approach a nearby house.

extract:primary-0007-eca4f3b3a3.summary: Alice joins the March Hare, Hatter, and Dormouse at a disorderly tea table. Their riddles, arguments about meaning and Time, and the Dormouse’s interrupted story increasingly frustrate her, so she leaves, reenters the long hall, and finally reaches the beautiful garden.

passages.title: The accusation
passages.text:
“The Queen of Hearts, she made some tarts,

 All on a summer day:

The Knave of Hearts, he stole those tarts,

 And took them quite away!”
passages.speaker: White Rabbit
passages.context: The White Rabbit reads the formal accusation after the King orders the herald to begin.
passages.significance: The verse states the charge at the center of the trial and identifies both the alleged victim and the accused.

plotBeats: Alice arrives at the crowded court and identifies the King as judge and the assembled creatures as jurors.
The White Rabbit reads the accusation that the Knave of Hearts stole the Queen’s tarts.
The King calls the Hatter, whose confused testimony is interrupted by threats and disputes.
A second witness refuses to cooperate and disappears while the court expels the Dormouse.
Alice grows larger and is called as the next witness.
openQuestions: What evidence will Alice give after the White Rabbit calls her as the next witness?

extract:primary-0012-e55373cbf3.summary: Alice’s sudden growth disrupts the court, but she rejects its arbitrary rules and unsupported evidence. The King of Hearts and Queen of Hearts press the case against the Knave of Hearts until Alice denounces them as cards and wakes beside her sister, realizing Wonderland was a dream.

entities.name: Alice
entities.summary: Alice gives evidence, challenges the court’s reasoning, and finally defies the card court before waking.
entities.excerpt: “Stuff and nonsense!” said Alice loudly.

claims.text: Alice rejects the proposal to impose a sentence before reaching a verdict.
claims.excerpt:
“The idea of having the sentence
first!”

entities.name: King of Hearts
entities.summary: The King conducts the proceedings, invents a rule aimed at Alice, and strains to interpret the verses as evidence.
entities.excerpt: “Read them,” said the King.

entities.summary: The Queen declares the Knave guilty, demands sentencing before a verdict, and calls for Alice’s execution.

claims.text: The Queen proposes sentencing before the jury gives its verdict.
claims.excerpt: “Sentence first—verdict afterwards.”

entities.summary: The White Rabbit corrects the King, presents a newly found paper, and reads its verses aloud.

claims.excerpt: “It isn’t a letter, after all: it’s a set of verses.”

passages.title: Alice rejects the card court
passages.speaker: Alice
passages.text:
“Who cares for you?” said Alice, (she had grown to her full size by this time).
“You’re nothing but a pack of cards!”
passages.context: Alice openly dismisses the court immediately before the cards fly at her and she wakes.
passages.significance: The declaration marks Alice’s final rejection of the court’s authority and precipitates the end of her dream.

plotBeats: Alice jumps up to give evidence and accidentally overturns the jury-box.
The King questions Alice and invents Rule Forty-two to make her leave the court.
The White Rabbit produces and reads an unsigned set of verses that the King treats as evidence against the Knave.
The Queen demands sentence before verdict and orders Alice to be silent.
Alice calls the court a pack of cards, wakes beside her sister, and recounts her dream.
